description: Original design moves for product-specific differentiation, not templates to copy. Directions are selected by task fit and validated by real renders.

moves.title: Proof in the object
moves.focus: E-commerce product, physical material and fulfillment facts lead.
moves.lead: Close-up owned object evidence and scale reference before supporting copy.
moves.sequence: Material detail → size/comparison → use context → fulfillment facts → primary purchase.
moves.stress_states: out-of-stock, variant error, shipping details, long product name
moves.acceptance_question: Is the object immediately recognizable and correctly scaled?

moves.title: Editorial index
moves.focus: Turn true history, chronology and named people into typography-led navigation.
moves.lead: Context-rich headline and large editorial index, not decorative hero copy.
moves.sequence: Index/period → narrative chapters → source notes → navigation.
moves.stress_states: long titles, missing images, keyboard navigation
moves.acceptance_question: Can an unfamiliar reader orient without the logo?

moves.title: Comparative proof
moves.focus: Make measurable differences and conditions visible side-by-side.
moves.lead: Comparison table with criteria and honest scope labels.
moves.sequence: Decision context → comparison → evidence → qualification → CTA.
moves.stress_states: missing feature, long value, narrow table, unavailable plan
moves.acceptance_question: Can a buyer explain the differences and limitations in a minute?

moves.title: Interactive workbench
moves.focus: Let the actual tool and its output replace marketing decoration.
moves.lead: Input/preview split that becomes stacked task flow on narrow screens.
moves.stress_states: invalid input, partial result, offline, mobile keyboard
moves.acceptance_question: Can the user complete the task without scrolling past a hero?

moves.title: Process as story
moves.focus: Explain why the work exists through original process evidence.
moves.lead: Original making/process shots anchored by real steps and timings.
moves.sequence: Result → stages → materials → maker notes → next action.
moves.stress_states: missing media, captions, reduced-motion, translated text
moves.acceptance_question: Would changing the product name break this story?

moves.title: Spatial exhibit
moves.focus: Use place and space as the navigation metaphor when the content genuinely has places.
moves.lead: Large map/space-context section with persistent wayfinding.
moves.sequence: Place context → destinations → details → practical information.
moves.stress_states: map unavailable, small screens, keyboard map alternative
moves.acceptance_question: Does the spatial layout simplify real navigation?

moves.title: Purposeful catalogue
moves.focus: Let precise categories and filters define the visual system.
moves.lead: Typographic category index with high-quality search and preview.
moves.stress_states: zero results, pagination, sorting, narrow viewport
moves.acceptance_question: Can the visitor identify scope, filters and next action?

moves.title: One clear choice
moves.focus: A concise thesis with one task-specific action and credible proof.
moves.lead: Specific product promise aligned to real interface or use evidence.
moves.stress_states: validation, consent, narrow fold, no network
moves.acceptance_question: Could the page be used by any competitor by only changing its logo?

moves.title: Operations console
moves.focus: Put scope, filter, high-impact decision and table before vanity statistics.
moves.lead: Scoped work queue/table with one contextual inspection panel.
moves.stress_states: empty, stale, permission, bulk action, long SKUs
moves.acceptance_question: Does every chart or KPI lead to an action?

moves.title: Camera instrument
moves.focus: Camera/capture occupies the screen; everything else is a reachable control.
moves.lead: Live capture with thumb-oriented primary control and status.
moves.stress_states: camera denied, slow capture, landscape, one-handed
moves.acceptance_question: Can the capture task start without entering generic navigation?

moves.title: Personal chronology
moves.focus: Entries and moments define structure, not generic dashboard tiles.
moves.lead: Date rhythm, content legibility and unmistakable edit status.
moves.stress_states: no entries, unsaved edit, long text, offline
moves.acceptance_question: Is personal media protected from distracting chrome?

moves.title: Focused creation
moves.focus: Make the work in progress dominant, with tools contextual to selection.
moves.lead: Large working canvas with inspector, commands and saved states.
moves.stress_states: empty canvas, unsaved, undo, narrow device
moves.acceptance_question: Does UI help the creation instead of crowding it?

moves.title: Honest ledger
moves.focus: Use accounting-like alignment when accurate amounts and history are the goal.
moves.lead: Amount, period, source and comparison explicitly aligned.
moves.stress_states: negative values, no data, currency, stale
moves.acceptance_question: Could a user reconcile each visible number to a source?

moves.title: Conversation craft
moves.focus: Identity and conversation context drive readable exchange and recovery.
moves.lead: Thread owns primary view; composer with precise send state.
moves.stress_states: long message, offline, attachments, keyboard
moves.acceptance_question: Is failed delivery obvious and recoverable?

moves.title: Adaptive inspector
moves.focus: High-density list becomes a contextual detail surface across widths.
moves.lead: List/detail split with visible selected context, stack on mobile.
moves.stress_states: no selection, zero matches, deep link, keyboard
moves.acceptance_question: Can the user find and resolve one item without losing scope?

moves.title: Single-purpose result
moves.focus: Complete a short utility task with minimal navigation and unambiguous result.
moves.lead: Input and big result first; context only when it changes an action.
moves.stress_states: invalid, permission, copied, small device
moves.acceptance_question: Can the task be done without a tutorial?

moves.title: Threat-first combat HUD
moves.focus: Critical enemy cues and player state outrank decoration.
moves.lead: Large clean playfield with danger cues and peripheral status.
moves.sequence: Playing → low HP → hit → pause → death/retry.
moves.stress_states: projectile clutter, color-blind, screen shake, lag
moves.acceptance_question: Do critical threats remain legible at full-speed playback?

moves.title: Rhythm clarity
moves.focus: Timing windows and lane legibility outrank spectacle.
moves.lead: Timing lane, note approach and grade feedback with sparse surrounding HUD.
moves.stress_states: frame drops, high speed, low vision, latency
moves.acceptance_question: Can timing and feedback be read without audio alone?

moves.title: Life in the scene
moves.focus: World activity drives tools and rewards rather than app-like cards.
moves.lead: Original living world with contextual inventory and gentle feedback.
moves.stress_states: small touch targets, item overflow, interrupted save
moves.acceptance_question: Is the world visually dominant during actual play?

moves.title: Strategic foresight
moves.focus: The map, consequences and previewability are the visual story.
moves.lead: Readable board with selection preview and controlled action panel.
moves.stress_states: dense units, selected/focus distinction, controller
moves.acceptance_question: Can players predict an action outcome before committing?

moves.title: Meaningful collecting
moves.focus: Item identity, rarity semantics and quick comparison define inventory.
moves.lead: Item silhouettes, comparison slots, explicit state, no surprise sales CTA.
moves.stress_states: full inventory, duplicate, controller, long names
moves.acceptance_question: Can players compare items without interpreting decoration?

moves.title: Finish and retry
moves.focus: Make death/win consequences and restart fast and understandable.
moves.lead: Large achieved result, meaningful feedback and clearly differentiated retry.
moves.stress_states: zero rewards, long stats, accidental purchase
moves.acceptance_question: Does the result communicate what changed and how to play again?

moves.title: World as UI
moves.focus: Use in-world artifacts if they improve immersion without hiding actions.
moves.lead: World artifact / map plus accessible operational overlay.
moves.stress_states: small script font, missing lore, controller and localization
moves.acceptance_question: Can players still read tasks at stressful moments?

moves.title: Crisp arcade instrumentation
moves.focus: Let time, rank and reward information compete only when needed.
moves.lead: Peripheral score instrumentation and one clear high-priority action region.
moves.stress_states: high score overflow, fast motion, pause
moves.acceptance_question: Is input, threat and score legible in a single glance?
